land.text: Medina and the Hejaz; Arabia re-united under the caliph in the Ridda wars (633)

successors.note: Infobox of the Rashidun page: 'Preceded by: First Islamic state'.

capitals.name: Medina
capitals.note: Where Muhammad settled in 622 and died in 632; the page does not call Medina a capital in those words.

rulers.name: Muhammad
rulers.title: prophet and head of the community

correction.text: 622-629: Medina and its oasis, the Muslim community's city

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has nothing before 633): the city of Medina and its oasis from the Hijra in 622 to the eve of the conquest of Mecca. The page names the city only.

New keyframe: from January 630 Mecca is Muslim, so the Hejaz is the core (the Medina page calls Mecca 'a dominant force in the Hejaz' without stating Medina's authority over the whole region). 'Most of the Arabian Peninsula had converted' (Muhammad page) is conversion, not control: Ridda wars follow.

ledger.note: 622: Muhammad settles at Medina and founds the first Islamic state. 'Muhammad came to the city of Medina following the migration of his followers in what is known as the Hijrah in 622'; the page links the Constitution of Medina to the 622 founding of the first Islamic state but says its date is 'debated'. The page gives no month for the Hijra.

region.text: the Hejaz between Medina and Mecca, the ground of the Muslim-Quraysh war

ledger.note: 622-629: 'eight years of intermittent fighting with Meccan tribes' (Muhammad page, written of December 629). The page I read dates no single battle on the Hejaz ground; the Medina page has Badr in 624 and the siege of Medina from 31 March 627. The zone is the Hejaz, my reading.

Jan 630: Mecca is taken. The infobox dates the conquest 'December 629 - January 630' (Ramadan 8 AH), the Muhammad page lists it under 630, the Medina page has Muhammad leaving 'around October 629'; the entry day is 'variously given'. 'The conquest went largely uncontested' and a general amnesty followed. The year is therefore 629/630; January 630 is used.
Jan 630: the infobox gives 'End of Muslim-Quraysh War'. The Hudaybiyyah pact of 628 had been breached 'in 630 (8 A.H.)' (page wording).

region.text: the Hejaz, the core of the state at Muhammad's death

ledger.note: 632: Muhammad dies in Medina. 'He died on Monday, June 8, 632, in the city'; the Rashidun Caliphate was founded in 632 under his companions, the Rightly Guided Caliphs. The Muhammad page says 'most of the Arabian Peninsula had converted to Islam' by his death; the extent of Medina's actual authority is not on any page I read, and the Ridda wars that followed re-united Arabia only in 633.

wars.name: Muslim-Quraysh War

zones.text: the Hejaz between Medina and Mecca

wars.outcome: Muslim victory: Mecca taken in December 629 - January 630, 'End of Muslim-Quraysh War'.
wars.note: Badr 624, the siege of Medina from 31 March 627, Hudaybiyyah in Shawwal 628 (Medina page).

certainty.note: A city-state and then a tribal confederation; no boundary on any page.

notes: Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19 from three pages. State Cliopatria lacks (its Rashidun row starts 633). Not on the pages: the Constitution of Medina's year, the Battles of Hunayn and Ta'if and the Tabuk expedition (the Medina page has Tabuk 'received the submission of some of the local chiefs', undated), the Year of Delegations, Muhammad's governors in Yemen, Bahrain and Oman, and the true extent of authority at death. A gap-filler could open 'Expedition of Tabuk' and 'Year of Delegations'. Counterpart 'Quraysh of Mecca' has no dossier (a city, not a state). The Rashidun dossier of this group begins from this state's Hejaz core in 632.
